slice: P3 AC1027 unmarked MATERIAL normal-map Scene-to-File plus filename transaction

scope.profile: One unchanged runtime-authored AC1027 MATERIAL profile with a complete diffuse/refraction prefix, inferred complete normal tuple, both outer group-72 source fields, and both group-3 filenames.
scope.operation: Change the selected normal source from 0 to 1 and replace only its group-3 filename in the same export transaction.
scope.encodingMatrix: ASCII and binary source, each exported as ASCII and binary DXF.

contract.admission: Only the selected unchanged source profile is admitted. The normal selector target must be 1 when its filename changes; procedural fields, luminance/explicit normal-strength profiles, other typed field edits, changed raw bodies, and unsupported source profiles remain refused.
contract.output: The physical output retains the diffuse group-72 selector and first group-3 filename, writes the normal group-72 selector as 1 and the second group-3 filename as the requested UTF-8 value, and leaves the other checked normal tuple fields unchanged. Fresh libdxfrw readback matches the full represented model.
contract.atomicity: A conflicting raw normal group-72 value refuses while preserving the destination sentinel and caller's requested source/file values. Restoring the captured raw body permits same-adapter retry and successful readback.

sourceBindings.fixture: Generated at runtime by tests/material_normal_role_tests.cpp from scratch; no DWG/DXF fixture is committed.

validation.focusedControls: Four positive ASCII/binary source/output combinations, exact physical fields, fresh readback, four conflicting-source refusals with destination/caller preservation, and four same-adapter retries.

references.title: Autodesk MaterialMap Source enumeration
references.use: The enum members are Scene, File, Procedural in that order; this supports the selected 0-to-1 field transition.

limitations: This proves selected DXF field transport, identity, readback, refusal, rollback, and retry only. It does not prove native image lookup, file availability, map evaluation, rendering, or whole-document conversion.
No procedural-source coupling, other source-profile boundary, other version, DWG path, or support claim is promoted.
